name: Small Business Security Readiness
description: A quick self-assessment of how well a small team protects its accounts, data and devices, with practical next steps per area.

thresholds.label: High risk
thresholds.summary: Several basic protections are missing. An attacker would not need advanced skills to cause real damage.

thresholds.label: Moderate risk
thresholds.summary: The foundations are in place, but there are gaps that are worth closing before they are tested by an incident.

thresholds.label: Well protected
thresholds.summary: Strong baseline. Focus on keeping these practices consistent as the team and tooling grow.

categories.name: Accounts & Access
categories.description: Who can sign in to what, and how well those accounts are protected.

recommendations.high-risk: Turn on multi-factor authentication for email and admin accounts first, then remove shared logins.
recommendations.moderate: Extend MFA to every business system and review who still has admin rights they no longer need.
recommendations.protected: Review access quarterly and remove accounts on the same day someone leaves.

questions.label: Is multi-factor authentication enabled for email and admin accounts?
Do people share logins for business tools?
How consistently does the team use a password manager?
When someone leaves, how quickly is their access removed?

options.label: We do not have a process

categories.name: Data Protection
categories.description: Backups and how sensitive information is stored and shared.

recommendations.high-risk: Set up automatic backups with one copy kept offline, and test a restore this month.
recommendations.moderate: Test restores on a schedule and move sensitive files out of personal accounts.
recommendations.protected: Document your backup and retention policy so it survives staff changes.

questions.label: How often are business-critical files backed up?
How many days ago did you last test restoring a backup?
Are laptops and phones with business data encrypted?

categories.name: Devices & Updates
categories.description: Keeping laptops, phones and software patched and protected.

recommendations.high-risk: Enable automatic updates on every device and remove software that is no longer supported.
recommendations.moderate: Keep an inventory of devices so nothing is left unpatched or unmanaged.
recommendations.protected: Keep doing this. Consider central device management as the team grows.

questions.label: How reliably are operating system and browser updates installed?
Do you keep a list of all devices used for work?

categories.name: Incident Readiness
categories.description: Knowing what to do when something goes wrong.

recommendations.high-risk: Write a one-page plan: who to call, how to lock accounts, and where backups live.
recommendations.moderate: Run a short phishing-awareness session and walk through the plan once with the team.
recommendations.protected: Rehearse the plan yearly and update contacts after any team change.

questions.label: Is there a written plan for a security incident?
How confident is the team at spotting phishing emails?
Anything else the assessor should know?

report.title: Security Readiness Scorecard
report.intro: This scorecard summarises the answers given in the self-assessment. Each area is scored from 0 to 100 using the rules defined in the assessment configuration, with a recommended next step for each.
report.footer: Generated with Scorecard Studio. Self-assessment only; not a substitute for a professional security audit.
